Overview

Problem statement SIH1741 — centralized application firewall
POLICY ENGINE ACTIVE · 3 ENDPOINTS ONLINE
? —
SIH1741
HARD

Centralized application-context aware firewall

Develop an application firewall for endpoints that can identify and restrict access of an application to external destinations based on context — not just IP or port. Sentrywall enforces per-application, per-destination policy at the endpoint, ships a live console for security teams, and flags behavior that deviates from an app's learned baseline.

What Sentrywall does

Four capabilities that map directly onto the problem statement
01 · IDENTIFY

Per-app context

Every outbound request is tagged with the requesting process, not just the source IP — so policy can say "Chrome may reach Google, Notepad may reach nothing."

02 · RESTRICT

Zero-trust default

Unmatched traffic is blocked by default. Access is only granted by an explicit allow rule on domain, wildcard, or protocol/port.

03 · DETECT

Baseline anomalies

Each app's traffic volume is profiled over time; a sudden spike or a connection to an unregistered destination raises an alert.

04 · MANAGE

Fleet-wide console

Security teams edit policy once and push it to every managed endpoint, with a live decision log for audits.

Suggested stack

What this prototype implies for the full build
Endpoint agent — Rust / eBPF (Linux) or WFP driver (Windows) Local policy engine — embedded rule cache, offline-first Control plane — REST/gRPC policy sync Anomaly model — lightweight per-app baseline (EWMA / isolation forest) Console — this dashboard

System architecture

How the pieces in this demo map to a real deployment

This console simulates the local policy engine that would run on every managed endpoint. In a production build, a lightweight agent intercepts outbound connections at the OS network layer, evaluates them against a locally-cached policy (so protection survives being offline), and reports decisions and traffic baselines back to a central console like this one.

01

Intercept

Agent hooks outbound socket calls at the OS layer and tags each with the initiating process.

02

Evaluate

Request is matched against the endpoint's cached, per-app rule set — default is deny.

03

Baseline

Traffic volume and destinations are compared against the app's learned normal behavior.

04

Report & sync

Decisions and anomalies stream to the console; new policy pushes flow back down to every endpoint.

🧩 Working enforcement prototype

This dashboard demonstrates the policy engine and console half of the architecture above. The Endpoint Agent box is implemented for real as the accompanying Sentrywall Enforcer browser extension (MV3) — it uses declarativeNetRequest to actually block navigation to disallowed domains system-wide inside the browser, before the request leaves the machine. Load it as an unpacked extension to see real GitHub/Facebook blocking, independent of this page.
